ranked.headline: Integrating single-cell and spatial data to infer regulatory and spatial organization
ranked.summary: Preprints and publications apply graph learning and optimal transport across multimodal single-cell and spatial data.

ranked.headline: Omics models make goals, decompositions and cross-species transfer explicit for testing
ranked.summary: Recent omics studies evaluate structural modeling decisions, such as subgroup goals and signature decomposition, rather than accepting them as defaults.

ranked.headline: Simulations test protein conformational ensembles against experimental observables
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications extend observable-constrained modeling to disordered regions, membrane complexes, and condensate-forming systems.

ranked.headline: Benchmarked computational methods for copy number and variant effect interpretation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers extend variant interpretation to copy number in repetitive regions, calibrated effect scores, and pharmacogenomics.

ranked.headline: New statistical methods resolve localized gene co-expression and spatial interactions
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers add spatially aware statistical models that account for spatial dependence and axis-specific measurement error.

ranked.headline: Benchmarked sequencing workflows for nanopore, TCR repertoire, and primer design
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers pair new sequencing methods with explicit reference testing, from nanopore consensus pipelines to TCR repertoire profiling.

ranked.headline: Context-resolved inference of regulatory and repair mechanisms in disease genomes
ranked.summary: Sequence-based models and single-cell profiling now resolve methylation, enhancer activity, and repair mechanisms at locus, cell, and pathway resolution.

ranked.headline: Network and topological structure replacing gene-level values in omics disease analysis
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a 2025 paper treat expression data as topological or network objects to recover disease-relevant structure beyond individual gene values.

ranked.headline: Learned molecular predictors evaluated under cross-chemical and cold-start splits
ranked.summary: Transfer-oriented evaluation now tests whether learned drug and toxicity predictors generalize across chemicals, species, and cold-start conditions.

ranked.headline: Long-read sequencing resolves haplotype, isoform and structural variant context
ranked.summary: Long-read and single-cell methods now resolve haplotypes, isoforms and structural variants across tumors, individual cells and brain transcriptomes.

ranked.headline: Shared embeddings and geometric coupling bridge spatial and multi-omics modalities
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple spatial transcriptomics slices and multi-omics modalities through alignment-aware embeddings, graph structure, and transformer adapters.

ranked.headline: Simulation and inference models link cellular state transitions to disease and aging
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair mechanistic simulation and statistical inference with spatial and survival data to test cellular and tissue-scale dynamics.

ranked.headline: Protein language model embeddings localize motifs and infer local structural similarity
ranked.summary: Pretrained protein language model embeddings now localize motifs, reveal local structural similarity, and enable remote homology search from sequence alone.

ranked.headline: Learned models are coupling biomolecular structure to explicit physical parametrizations
ranked.summary: Recent preprints probe how torsion, coordinate, and electron-density parametrizations shape learned biomolecular models; all results are unverified.

ranked.headline: Recovering latent epidemiological quantities from indirect biological measurements
ranked.summary: Routinely collected surveillance and clinical streams now support probabilistic inference of latent epidemiological quantities.

ranked.headline: Structure-guided computational design of peptide, antibody, and enzyme variants
ranked.summary: Chirality-agnostic peptide design and energy-guided antibody co-optimization extend structure-based design to D-peptides and affinity-stability trade-offs.

ranked.headline: Deep learning and taxonomy-aware models are extending genomic and microbiome inference
ranked.summary: Learned representations now reach gene annotation, viral relationship inference, and microbiome trait modeling, with benchmarks probing LLM reliability.

ranked.headline: Gene regulatory inference methods add isoform, network, and regulatory-input context
ranked.summary: Items dated 22–26 November 2025 extend regulatory inference beyond single-gene differential expression to isoform, network, and promoter context.

ranked.headline: Graph and alignment structures extend genomic analysis beyond linear references
ranked.summary: Graph-based and bias-corrected methods are addressing multi-sample metagenomics, population ancestry, and phylogenetic confidence in recent work.

ranked.headline: Integrating bulk, single-cell, and multi-tissue data to sharpen QTL and TWAS inference
ranked.summary: Population-scale whole-genome, transcriptome, and single-cell cohorts now enable cross-tissue and cell-type-resolved QTL models linked to GWAS.

ranked.headline: Scalable methods now reach genome-wide ARG, species-tree, alignment and diversity analyses
ranked.summary: Biobank-scale and species-scale genomic datasets demand tools that bound memory and exploit parallel hardware, as these preprints and papers demonstrate.

ranked.headline: Learned models tackle missingness and sparse counts in omics and histology data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply masked autoencoders, negative binomial models, and foundation models to incomplete or sparse omics data.

ranked.headline: Structured models of brain connectivity capture higher-order and dynamical properties
ranked.summary: Recent work moves beyond raw neural signals toward inferred structured objects, from fMRI combinatorial complexes to network control of timescales.

ranked.headline: State-transition models of protein aggregation, epidemic waves, and actin selection
ranked.summary: Three November 2025 preprints add phase-plane, distributed-memory, and finite-pool models of state transitions across molecular and population scales.

ranked.headline: Calibrating mechanistic models against tree-structured and dynamical data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend calibration and comparison of mechanistic models to transmission trees, phylogenies, and dynamical trajectories.

ranked.headline: Software tools refine microbial taxonomy, SNP prioritization and host-read removal
ranked.summary: Shotgun, amplicon and WGS datasets increasingly require reproducible, host-filtered and primer-aware processing before biological interpretation.

ranked.headline: Interpretable sequence models decode motif syntax and RNA-RNA interactions
ranked.summary: Architectures aligned with motif or pairwise sequence structure are being applied to enhancers, transcription factors, and miRNA targeting.

ranked.headline: Open-source tools automate omics preprocessing, feature extraction and biomarker modeling
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications release open packages for spatial, surface-marker, multimodal, and sequence-embedding data analysis.

ranked.headline: Chromosome-level genomes reveal introgression and posthybridization genome evolution
ranked.summary: Chromosome-level assemblies across whiptail lizards and Drosophila now allow hybridization, introgression, and chromosome evolution to be resolved directly.

ranked.headline: New reference genomes for oyster, plover, dolphin and springtail with annotation
ranked.summary: Four new non-model animal genome assemblies add reference resources for comparative analyses of selection and gene family evolution.

ranked.headline: Pangenome graphs improve SNP and structural variant detection in pathogen genomes
ranked.summary: Graph-based and mutation-level tools are now applied to large pathogen datasets, including 6.6M SARS-CoV-2 genomes and 859 Mtb long-read assemblies.

ranked.headline: Deep learning tools now segment membranes, cryo-EM particles and protein puncta
ranked.summary: Pretrained and fine-tuned segmentation models are being applied to cryo-EM, cryo-ET and 4D protein microscopy data, alongside large structural resources.

ranked.headline: Learned representations of protein structure and sequence for binding and epitope tasks
ranked.summary: Representation choices for protein sequence and structure are now benchmarked across binding, epitope, and database search tasks.

ranked.headline: Index-based k-mer search and parsing tools target million-genome and FASTQ workloads
ranked.summary: Laptop-scale and memory-bounded indexing now make million-genome k-mer search and gzipped FASTQ parsing feasible without recompressing data.

ranked.headline: Antibody-antigen structures and databases reveal convergent binding and immune escape
Stochastic models link noise and transport to cell-scale outcomes in expression and…
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply stochastic models to chemotactic migration, gene expression noise, and reaction network dynamics at cellular scales.

ranked.headline: Learned sequence models target RNA design and RNA-protein binding energetics
ranked.summary: Three November 2025 preprints couple language-model or graph-based sequence modeling with structural or binding objectives for RNA design.

ranked.headline: MD simulations map allosteric and DNA-processing mechanisms across three systems
ranked.summary: Microsecond MD and chain-of-replicas path optimization now tie simulated ensembles to quantitative mechanistic readouts.

ranked.headline: Computational corrections extend what proteomic and imaging experiments can resolve
ranked.summary: Pairing multiplexed imaging, stable isotope labeling, and deuterated water labeling with new analysis pipelines expands what protein-level experiments can…

ranked.headline: Software now visualizes parental genome contribution, gene loss and recombination graphs
ranked.summary: Interactive and command-line tools now expose genome structure from assemblies, crosses and genealogies for direct inspection.
